clues: This place stands in a region of four lakes, with two big lakes close by its downtown. Woods and wet swamp once covered the ground here.
Winters here plunge far below freezing, with snow that can pile deep. Summers then swing back to warm days, a huge change in one year.
In 1836, lawmakers met to pick a lasting home for their government. One man won them over with warm buffalo robes and cheap lots in his new town.
Downtown here sits on a thin strip of land with a lake on each side. You can stand in the middle and see water both ways.
The lawmakers of Wisconsin meet in this place to make state laws. They gather in the state capitol, the house of state government.
